evals.name: async-upload-pipeline-full-loop
evals.prompt: I've got a service in ./svc with a docker-compose.yml that also brings up Kafka and Azurite, and I collected the docs into ./docs. Can you set up end-to-end tests for this and actually run them? I want to know the upload flow really works, not just that the endpoint returns something.
evals.expected_output: A working E2E suite: e2e/inventory.json listing kafka + azure-storage + the service, e2e/journeys.json with at least one journey asserting on the async effects (blob and/or Kafka message), generated Playwright specs, and a run that boots the stack, passes, and tears down.
assertions: Discovered Kafka and blob storage as distinct resources, not just the HTTP service
At least one test asserts on the Kafka message produced by the upload
At least one test asserts on the blob written to storage
Assertions wait for the async effect by polling, rather than a fixed sleep
The test suite was actually executed against running containers, not just generated
All generated tests pass
Containers were torn down after the run
The upload id from the POST response is carried into the later async assertions

evals.name: refuses-ungrounded-journeys
evals.prompt: Set up e2e tests for the system in this folder. There's a docker-compose.yml with the services. Go ahead and build the test suite.
evals.expected_output: Notices there is no documentation folder, and either stops to ask / offers to collect docs first, or explicitly names the --allow-no-docs tradeoff before proceeding. Does not silently invent journeys.
assertions: Noticed and stated that no documentation folder is present
Surfaced the missing-docs decision to the user rather than silently inventing journeys
Named the concrete tradeoff of proceeding without docs (tests describe what the code does, not what it promises)
Any journeys it did write are traceable to the code it actually read
Did not claim the suite is grounded in documentation

evals.name: extends-existing-suite-new-journey
evals.prompt: The e2e harness is already wired up for this repo. The docs describe a status endpoint that flips from 404 to 200 once an upload is processed, but I don't think we cover it. Add a journey for that and make sure it passes.
evals.expected_output: Adds a journey using await_http (not sleep) to poll /uploads/{id} until 200, validates it, rebuilds, and runs. Does not hand-edit the generated spec files.
assertions: Added coverage for GET /uploads/{id} flipping from 404 to 200
The new coverage polls until the status changes rather than sleeping a fixed duration
Edited the journeys source of truth, not the generated spec files
Regenerated the tests after editing rather than hand-writing them
The suite was run and the new coverage passes
Existing journeys still pass (no regression)
Containers were torn down after the run
